scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
**Artifact family: an executive summary**

You are measured on cutting your firm's $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on walking into a DOT compliance audit that opens in six months with a clean result. Today that spend runs through 28 on-premises Microsoft SQL Server instances hosted across 620 Hyper-V virtual machines, carrying your load-matching and carrier-settlement systems — the two systems a DOT auditor will ask about first. [PF-2.11 GAP: no stated target reduction in annual run-rate — the buyer has not yet specified a savings percentage or dollar target to measure the programme against] You need the ability to run those systems on infrastructure you can scale and audit on demand, rather than on fixed hardware you provision for peak load year-round; Google Compute Engine and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL are the means proposed to deliver that, replacing the 28 SQL Server instances and 620 VMs with managed compute and a managed database layer over a two-year, $4,200,000 programme. [PF-1.14 GAP: the $1,850,000 and 620-VM/28-instance figures are stated as the buyer's current baseline, but no source document or measurement date has been supplied to attribute them to]

[PF-2.17 REVIEW (compliance): the programme is described as improving DOT audit readiness, but no named control, certification, or audit-trail capability has been confirmed to map to the DOT's specific data-retention and traceability requirements] Over the two years, you should expect a phased cutover of load-matching and carrier-settlement workloads off Hyper-V and SQL Server onto Compute Engine and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, with each of the 28 instances and 620 VMs retired on a named schedule rather than in a single cutover. [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): "you should expect" language describing scope and sequencing may be read as a delivery commitment and should be confirmed against the contracted statement of work before this ships] [PF-1.17 GAP: no named, checkable comparable — a prior migration of similar scale for a freight brokerage or comparable on-prem SQL Server/Hyper-V estate — has been supplied to evidence that this vendor has executed a migration of this size before]

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| No stated savings target | PF-2.11 | The CFO's specific reduction target (%, $) against the $1,850,000 baseline |
| No source/date for baseline figures | PF-1.14 | Attribution for the $1,850,000 spend and 28-instance/620-VM count (which document, as of when) |
| DOT audit-readiness compliance claim | PF-2.17 | Confirmation of which specific control or certification maps to DOT audit requirements |
| "You should expect" sequencing language | PF-2.14 | Confirmation this reads as scope description, not a contractual delivery commitment |
| No named comparable migration | PF-1.17 | A named, checkable prior migration of comparable scale to cite as proof |
